source_conclusions: Transport diff contains observation hooks only, no descriptor, accepting condition, PID, deadline, credit, receipt or controlled-port change; diagnostic state appended after existing members.

TX helper reads retained wire after successful publication and before wipe; software callback return cannot affect acceptance. EID0f helper reads copied checked body before rearm, no retained packet pointer.

RX helper reads copied rx_frame only after actual descriptor rearm and before next receive overwrite/callback. It counts validated native Ethernet, not BSD ifnet_input success. Supplemental rejecting-consumer callback proves this distinction: RX count increments after rearm even though consumer failure then halts/closes via existing path.

IP/UDP/BOOTP/options bounds prevent reads beyond supplied extents. Fragmented/overloaded/malformed/duplicate/missing DHCP types become diagnostic unknown. Checksums, transaction identity, server authenticity and lease status are deliberately unproved.

Independent4/12 TX/RX header classes and8/16 TXS reservations cap85 lines; summary freezes counters, all numeric increments/sums saturate. Every header is atomic printf; DATATXS split pair has same numeric n.
Original EVENT_TX_DONE88B/offsets/bit0 source independently compiled; advanced fields exposed only when flag valid. PID127 remains explicitly ambiguous, last publication is context only.
Registration patch baseline hashes match current canonical WPAHDR source lists. Existing WPA helper remains linked; scan-return uses updated join-owner runner.
limits: Actual native data/RF/DHCP lease/IP success not claimed.
Original-source oracle checks ABI and flag, not firmware availability or per-packet correlation.
Additional probe first draft had a fixture extent typo; corrected to include the zero-length option byte, then all269 probes passed; no runtime correction was required.
Parent must add required bsd/conf/files standard entry and run final generated/owning-TU composition before CI; author3-TU report inspected, not redundantly rerun.
